decisions.decision_summary: Open on a reader lost in an endless article, then hit them with: 'Never get lost in a long read again.'
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is a viral hook with high emotional stakes, and the commit backs a big but honest claim. It adds a reading progress bar and section navigation so readers see how far they are and can jump to any section. 'Never lost again' is the biggest line the diff supports. I'll back Dev to keep me factual, since the diff is a one-line single-file change and I won't invent extra features.
decisions.dialogue: Never get lost in a long read again. Smart Scroll shows where you are!

decisions.decision_summary: Open on a long article where the reader loses their place, then show only what the commit claims: a 6px progress bar and links to four sections, with no 'smart' or AI framing.
decisions.reasoning_why: The commit is one changed line in index.html, and the excerpt cuts off the added line. The removed version already had CSS for header, #bar and nav but no matching markup or script, so the diff alone shows no scroll logic. I'll only stand behind the commit message's two claims: a reading progress bar and jumping to sections (#attention, #rhythm, #clarity, #future). No personalization, no AI, no analytics. 'Smart' is just the branch name, and I expect Growth to lean on it.
decisions.dialogue: Open on a long page. Thin bar fills, four section links. That's the whole feature.

decisions.decision_summary: Open cold on a reader lost mid-article, then frame Smart Scroll as a skeptic's trial: one minified line must prove the bar and section jumps work.
decisions.reasoning_why: The diff is a single-line swap of minified index.html, and the excerpt cuts off the new version, so we can't see the bar or nav logic. The old file already styled header, #bar and nav, yet its markup had none of them. I'll press Dev to show the bar on camera. My planted edge case: does it reach 100% on the last section, or stall before the decision-log link?
decisions.dialogue: One line changed, Dev? Show me that bar hitting a hundred percent, or it's decor.

decisions.decision_summary: Open cold on an endless scrolling article with a lost reader, then snap in a thin green progress bar filling across the top, staying under 105 seconds.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is tight pacing and strong visuals. The commit promises exactly two things, a reading progress bar and jump-to-section navigation, so the opening must show those and nothing more. The diff is a one-line index.html swap and the new markup is truncated, so I'm backing Dev to keep us honest. No past endings exist, so we are free to build a fresh, decisive finish.
decisions.dialogue: Frame it: endless text, a lost reader, then one green line fills the sky!

decisions.decision_summary: I pick user_misuse: the first reader jumps straight to section 04 or has scripts off, and we watch whether the bar keeps up.
decisions.reasoning_why: In the diff, #bar starts at width:0, and the visible excerpt shows no script that updates it, because the new line is truncated. A reader who skips straight to '04 / The future' via a section link, or who browses with JavaScript disabled, is the edge case nobody in the room raised. Growth promised 'never get lost,' and Director wants the bar to fill the sky. This twist forces both claims to survive one real user on camera, without us inventing behavior the commit doesn't show.
decisions.dialogue: Reader clicks straight to section four. Bar says zero? Then 'never lost' just got lost.

decisions.decision_summary: Support the user-misuse twist, but only if the film never shows the bar failing or succeeding in ways the truncated diff doesn't prove.
decisions.reasoning_why: The twist tests Growth's 'never get lost' overclaim, which serves my goal. But the diff excerpt cuts off at '<!doct'. The old line has CSS for header, #bar and nav, but no header, nav or script markup. That means we can't see the new script's logic or how it behaves with scripts disabled. Section ids (attention, rhythm, clarity, future) are real, so a jump to 04 is fair to show. The bar's response to that jump has to stay unstated, not invented as a failure or a win.
decisions.dialogue: Fine, test it. But the diff's truncated. We show the jump, not invented bar behavior.

decisions.decision_summary: I oppose the 'Users use it wrong' twist because jumping straight to a section is the feature itself, not misuse, and the twist kills our hook.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is a bold, emotional hook. A twist built on the feature failing undercuts 'never get lost' in the opening line. The commit body says readers 'can jump to any section,' so clicking section 04 is the designed path, not an edge case. The diff excerpt cuts off before any script, so neither the Critic nor I can prove how the bar behaves after a jump. A film shouldn't stake its drama on an unshown failure. Better to show a reader landing on section 04 with the bar reflecting their place, if Dev confirms it works.
decisions.dialogue: Jumping to section four isn't misuse, Critic. That's the headline feature working!

decisions.decision_summary: I support the user-misuse twist as one tight mid-film beat: the reader jumps straight to section 04. I am cutting the scripts-off variant.
decisions.reasoning_why: A reader leaping to section 04 gives us a strong visual jolt and room for a decisive payoff. The commit body claims readers can jump to any section and see how far through they are, so the resolution is a beat about position, not an invented guarantee. The diff we have is truncated: the old line shows #bar at width:0 and no script, so we cannot prove how the bar behaves. Scripts-off would leave the ending unresolved or force us to fabricate behavior, so it goes. Budget the beat at about 15 seconds to stay inside 105. With no past endings, a fresh decisive close is ours to build.
decisions.dialogue: Yes! Reader leaps to section four. Hold on the bar. Fifteen seconds, then we land it.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote honest_caveat: ship it, and say out loud that the film shows only what the one-line diff verifiably contains.
decisions.reasoning_why: The merge is a single minified line, and the excerpt truncates the new version. The old line defines CSS for header and #bar at width:0 but shows no script, so the bar's behavior on a section jump isn't proven. Triumphant or critic_converted would claim behavior the diff doesn't show, and Growth's 'never get lost again' overclaims. The caveat keeps the film accurate.
decisions.dialogue: Ship it, but say it plainly: one-line diff, bar and links. No 'never lost' promises.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote critic_converted: Critic jumps straight to section four, the jump lands, and the skeptic becomes our loudest fan.
decisions.reasoning_why: My goal is high emotional stakes and a viral hook, and a converted skeptic is the strongest arc we have. It also stays honest. The commit body says readers 'can jump to any section,' and section links are the feature's core, so Critic's 'misuse' is really the headline use case. The diff is truncated, so I won't claim exact bar percentages. The conversion comes from the section jump the commit promises, and the bar filling as they read on.
decisions.dialogue: Critic tried to break it, jumped to section four, and landed. Now he's our biggest fan!

decisions.decision_summary: I vote honest_caveat: ship it, but say on camera that nobody has proven the bar tracks a direct jump to section 04.
decisions.reasoning_why: The diff is a single minified line, and the visible '+' side is truncated at '<!doct'. All we can see is the old page, where #bar sits at width:0 and no script is shown. So the film cannot show the bar keeping up after a straight-to-section-04 jump, and it cannot show it failing either. That deep-link edge case is the one Growth waved off as 'the headline feature working'. My goal is to expose it on camera, and saying it out loud is the only honest way. triumphant_launch and critic_converted would both claim a success the diff doesn't prove. fix_first would invent a bug we can't see. honest_caveat keeps the edge case in the film without lying in either direction.
decisions.dialogue: Applause? Nobody's proven the bar survives a deep link. Say that out loud, then ship.

decisions.decision_summary: I vote honest_caveat: it ships, and the final beat names what the truncated one-line diff can and cannot prove.
decisions.reasoning_why: Critic's section-04 jump needs a resolution we can stand behind. The visible diff shows a 6px bar starting at width 0 and links to four sections. The new line is truncated, so nothing shows the bar catching up after a jump. Critic_converted and triumphant_launch would both assert behavior we can't see. Fix_first invents a bug we can't prove. Honest_caveat is decisive, fits 90 seconds, and gives a strong closing visual: the reader lands on 04 and the room says plainly what was shipped. There are no past endings, so this sets our first one cleanly.
decisions.dialogue: Freeze on section four! We ship it, and say exactly what one line proves.

decisions.decision_summary: Final ending is honest_caveat: the film ships Smart Scroll and closes by naming exactly what the one-line diff shows and what it cannot prove.
decisions.reasoning_why: The weighted tally is decisive: honest_caveat 4.50 against critic_converted 1.50, with Dev, Critic and me aligned. My memory holds no past endings, so this repeats nothing. The diff is one minified line, truncated, in index.html. The removed version shows a 6px header bar and four sections, but the added line cuts off after '<!doct'. That means the film can't claim deep-link tracking or 'never lost'. The ending will freeze on section 04 with the bar visible, then print one plain caveat card. That is a clean, decisive close inside 105 seconds, and it doesn't spin the converted-critic fantasy Growth wanted.
decisions.dialogue: Freeze! Section four, thin green line. We ship it, and say what one line proves.
